description: FLAREFORGE is a team of tech and space enthusiasts at NASA Space Apps 2026. We aim to build FLARE-SI, an AI-powered platform that turns NASA microgravity combustion research into evidence based fire safety insights for spacecraft, Moon bases, and Mars habitats. We welcome teammates interested in Python, AI/ML, data analysis, web development, UI/UX, physics, aerospace, and research. Curiosity and teamwork matter most. Join us to make space exploration safer.
summary: FLAREFORGE (FLARE Intelligence) is an evidence grounded research workspace for exploring spacecraft fire safety research across prevention, detection, and suppression. It organizes four NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) source collections FLEX, BASS-II, SAFFIRE, and SAME-R into searchable records, investigation views, scientific summaries, comparisons, and data quality reports. Users can inspect source linked experimental records, compare selected SAFFIRE samples, review FLEX outcome distributions, explore SAME-R smoke-particle summaries, and assess which supplied evidence is relevant to a user defined mission scenario. A transparent heuristic ranks evidence relevance and reports missing coverage; it is not a fire risk probability or validated safety model. FLAREFORGE preserves source labels, missing values, campaign distinctions, and provenance so that unlike measurements are not presented as directly comparable. The prototype aims to make existing microgravity combustion research easier to discover, compare, and interpret.
details:
Project Details — FLAREFORGE

FLAREFORGE is a research platform designed to make spacecraft fire-safety research easier to explore and understand. The idea is to bring findings from different NASA microgravity combustion experiments into one place, so researchers can explore existing evidence without having to work through separate datasets individually.

The platform currently works with four NASA research collections: FLEX (274 records), BASS-II (129 records), SAFFIRE (11 curated sample rows), and SAME-R (10 material and aging summary rows). Together, these contain 424 entries. Since the collections have different structures and purposes, we preserve their original context rather than treating every entry as a directly comparable experiment.

Users can browse investigations, examine source records, explore interactive charts, compare selected research findings, and review data-quality information. The platform also includes an evidence graph, question answering capabilities, and a mission scenario tool that helps identify research findings relevant to a particular scenario. Its evidence-ranking feature uses a transparent heuristic to highlight matching variables, available coverage, and missing information. It is intended to support research exploration, not to predict fire risk or make operational safety decisions.

We also included an optional local AI integration using Ollama to help summarize retrieved research evidence. The underlying data and numerical analysis remain the primary sources of information.

One of our main priorities was to preserve the reliability of the original research. We retained source information, kept missing values visible, and avoided silently changing uncertain labels or measurement units.

FLAREFORGE is a research prototype.Our goal is to make existing space-combustion research more accessible and useful for future research into fire prevention, detection, and suppression.

Technology Stack: Python, FastAPI, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, NetworkX, Pandera, Next.js, React, Recharts, Plotly.js, and Three.js.
dataRefs: NASA BASS-II – Burning and Suppression of Solids (PSI-25)
NASA SAFFIRE – Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests (NTRS 20170008805)
NASA SAME-R – Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight (PSI-101)
